title: Noether normalization lifted to a Tate presentation
statement: Let $K$ be a complete field [def-weil-field] with a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value, let $T_r=K\langle T_1,\ldots,T_r\rangle$ be the restricted-series ring [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation], and let $I\subset T_r$ be a proper ideal. There are an integer $0\le d\le r$ and an injective $K$-algebra homomorphism $\iota:K\langle U_1,\ldots,U_d\rangle\to T_r$ such that its composite with $T_r\to T_r/I$ is injective and makes $T_r/I$ a finitely generated module over $K\langle U_1,\ldots,U_d\rangle$. For $d=0$ the source is $K$.

source.place: Section 1.2, Corollary 10 (Noether normalization), printed p.14, including its lifted monomorphism into the original Tate algebra. Primary PDF read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Induct on $r$, proving the assertion for every proper ideal of $T_r$. If $I=0$, take $d=r$ and the identity: the quotient is generated by $1$ over $T_r$. If $r=0$, then $T_0=K$ by [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation]; a nonzero element of a proper ideal would have an inverse in $K$, forcing $1$ into the ideal. Thus $I=0$, already covered. Now let $r\ge1$ and $I\ne0$.

source.place: Section 1.2, Corollary 10: induction, with zero ideal and zero-variable base made explicit.

proof.text: Choose $0\ne f\in I$. Apply [lem-per-tate-triangular-distinguished-coordinate] over this same complete nonarchimedean field $K$. Obtain an automorphism $\sigma$ and a unit $v\in T_{r-1}$ such that $g=v\sigma(f)=\sum a_jT_r^j$ has $a_s=1$, $\|a_j\|\le1$ for $j<s$, and $\sup_{j>s}\|a_j\|<1$. Put $I^{\prime}=\sigma(I)$ and $C=T_r/I^{\prime}$. Then $I^{\prime}$ is proper and contains $g$. By [lem-trf-tate-weierstrass-norm-division], every $h\in T_r$ is $qg+\sum_{j<s}b_jT_r^j$ with $b_j\in T_{r-1}$. Hence $C$ is generated by the classes $e_j=[T_r^j]$, $0\le j<s$, over $A=T_{r-1}$. If $s=0$, division gives $1=qg$, contradicting properness; therefore $s\ge1$.

source.place: Section 1.2, Corollary 10 first paragraph, using Lemma 7 and Theorem 8.

proof.text: Let $j:A\hookrightarrow T_r$ insert a zero exponent in the last coordinate of a restricted series [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation]; its coefficients show directly that it is an injective $K$-algebra map. Let $J=\ker(A\xrightarrow{j}T_r\to C)$. Since $1_C\ne0$, $J$ is proper. The map $\beta:A/J\to C$, $[a]\mapsto[j(a)]$, is injective by the definition of $J$. The spanning formula in step 2 also holds over $A/J$, since $J$ acts by zero on $C$. Apply the inductive hypothesis at $r-1$ to $J$: there are $d\le r-1$ and an injection $\lambda:T_d\to A$ whose reduction $\bar\lambda:T_d\to A/J$ is injective and finite.

source.place: Section 1.2, Corollary 10 second paragraph: contracted kernel and induction.

proof.text: Choose generators $b_1,\ldots,b_t$ of $A/J$ over $T_d$. For $c\in C$, step 2 gives $c=\sum_{j<s}\beta(\bar a_j)e_j$. Write $\bar a_j=\sum_{k=1}^t\bar\lambda(u_{jk})b_k$ with $u_{jk}\in T_d$. Substitution gives $c=\sum_{j,k}(\beta\bar\lambda)(u_{jk})\beta(b_k)e_j$, so the finitely many $\beta(b_k)e_j$ generate $C$ over $T_d$. Set $\iota=\sigma^{-1}j\lambda:T_d\to T_r$, a composite of injections. The map $\theta:C\to T_r/I$, $[h]\mapsto[\sigma^{-1}(h)]$, is well-defined with inverse $[h]\mapsto[\sigma(h)]$. For $u\in T_d$, $\theta((\beta\bar\lambda)(u))=[\iota(u)]$. Thus the quotient composite of $\iota$ is injective, and the images under $\theta$ of the displayed generators generate $T_r/I$ for exactly this scalar action. Finally $d\le r-1\le r$; when $d=0$ the source is $K$.

source.place: Section 1.2, Corollary 10: explicit product generators and lift back through the coordinate automorphism.

I fetched Bosch's heft378 PDF from source.url because the archival file is not in literature/ (WANTED; proof_origin agent is correct) and read Def. 6, Lemma 7, Thm 8, Cor. 9 and Cor. 10 with its proof (printed pp.10-14). The item statement equals Cor. 10 without the Krull-dimension clause, which no citer uses. Steps: (1) base cases r=0 (T_0=K, so a proper ideal is 0) and I=0 (identity). (2) The triangular node gives σ, v and g=vσ(f) with a_s=1, ‖a_j‖≤1 below s, sup‖a_j‖<1 above s, which are exactly the hypotheses of lem-trf-tate-weierstrass-norm-division with s=r-1 Y-variables. Division makes C=T_r/σ(I) generated by the T_r^j (j<s) over T_{r-1}, and s=0 is ruled out because then 1=qg. (3) The contracted kernel J is proper because C≠0; β is injective; induction applies to J. (4) Finiteness of the composite is written as an explicit double sum; ι=σ^{-1}jλ; θ is induced by σ^{-1}, so the quotient composite is θβλ̄, injective and finite. Small cases checked: r=1 with I=(T_1^2), (T_1-T_2), nonreduced ideals; I=T_r is excluded by the statement. No missing hypothesis. Duplicate search (rg -L over the snapshot DAG, blueprint_refs search) found no analytic-normalization node; same_as=[] is correct. Mathlib has only the basic restricted-series API and polynomial Noether normalization, so no match. lean.statement: theorem tate_normalization_lift (K : Type u) [NormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K] (hK : ∃ a : K, a ≠ 0 ∧ ‖a‖ ≠ 1) (r : ℕ) (I : Ideal ↥(MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring (R := K) (fun _ : Fin r ↦ (1 : ℝ)))) (hI : I ≠ ⊤) : ∃ d : ℕ, d ≤ r ∧ ∃ ι : ↥(MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring (R := K) (fun _ : Fin d ↦ (1 : ℝ))) →+* ↥(MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring (R := K) (fun _ : Fin r ↦ (1 : ℝ))), Function.Injective ι ∧ ι.comp (constants K d) = constants K r ∧ Function.Injective ((Ideal.Quotient.mk I).comp ι) ∧ ((Ideal.Quotient.mk I).comp ι).Finite
